newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga's Kristin oil find largest for a decade.
newsitem.headline: Saga's Kristin oil find largest for a decade.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Wednesday it had confirmed that its Kristin gas and condensate find off mid-Norway held reserves of at least 700 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe), making it one of the largest discoveries in Norwegian waters in 10 years.
Kristin is bigger than the nearby Lavrans prospect -- also operated by Saga -- which holds around 650 million boe.

"The important factor about Kristin is that this result is after just one well. We are planning to begin spudding a second well on June 1," Saga spokesman Petter Nore told Reuters. "There is an upside potential here, which we hope to see by mid-August or September."
Discovered in January, Kristin lies in block 6506/2 close to the Aasgard project under development and the Tyrihans prospect in the Haltenbanken area of the Norwegian Sea.
The main body of the reserve is covered by production licence 199 in which Saga holds 25 percent interest, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil ) 60 percent and Mobil 15 percent.
About 20 percent of the reservoir stretches into PL 134, which is held by Statoil with 53 percent, Agip with 30 percent, Total with 10 percent and Saga with seven percent.
Nore said the company planned to develop Kristin ahead of Lavrans because of the high level of liquids in the former.
"A key element is to get an allocation for gas supplies before a decision is made to develop. We are concentrating on Kristin because it has more liquids and therefore better economics," he said.
Saga plans to present a development plan to the authorities in spring, 1998. The field could come onstream in 2002 depending on gas sales allocations.

It also will evaluate this year the possibility of laying a pipeline to land condensate from the Haltenbank area. If implemented, the pipeline would be the first to shore light oil from this part of the Norwegian continental shelf.
